subject: Confirm the peer Loom session has finished and record the pre-refinement baseline; holds the protocol for every later task
description:
RESULT (2026-10-03):
- The peer session "loom implementation gaps" finished: 27 commits on Loom main up to 1f5217d, unpushed.
- Measured 12:44:32Z, AMC-D-PF3XTNPM: `git status --short` is empty; HEAD is 1f5217d; `## main` with no upstream; `SqlLocalDB info` lists only MSSQLLocalDB.
- BASELINE: the peer's final gate at that same unchanged, clean HEAD, as reported by the peer, not re-run.
  - Every suite exited 0.
  - workspace 43/43, qualification 47/47, cli 50/50, mcp 15/15, fixtures 59/59.
  - MCP smoke PASS on 12 tools; designer build and tests pass.
  - self-test: 20 of 20 required checks PASS.
  - coverage --check: 123 capabilities, 230 cases, 459 verified references, 0 findings.
  - docs --check: 0 findings.
  - The run record pins 1f5217d, not dirty, with contract digest sha256:8eb65147….
  - Task 28 compares against these figures.
- Tools/Context-Engineering before any refinement work (`git -C Tools/Context-Engineering status --porcelain`, 2026-10-03, AMC-D-PF3XTNPM): ` M Brainstorming.md`, `?? loomrefinements.md`, `?? skills/`, none of it written by this session. Task 28 compares against it.

GOAL (owner, 2026-10-04): deliver Loom 1.0.0 as loomrefinements.md specifies, in six milestones. Each milestone ends committed, pushed and usable, and within one the task order follows the plan gate's dependencies. A task's milestone is in its metadata.
- a: agent experience — 10, 14, 21, 22.
- b: composition — 11, 15, 35.
- c: diagrams — 30, 12, 13, 20, 31, 36.
- d: SQL qualification — 16, 17, 18, 27, 32, 19, 37.
- e: browser — 23, 24, 25.
- f: release — 26, 28.
- The last task of each of a–d carries a MILESTONE-END CHECK: the milestone's scenarios have current evidence at the layer the spec names, each with a negative control; then the plan gate, commit, push and superproject bump.
- Done: every scenario evidenced (the service provider reported unqualified); one clean full run with no regression; every capability entry complete; release evidence binding commit and working-tree hash; the plan gate maps every statement to a completed task; the spec SHA-256 unchanged; no commit of this session touches Tools/Context-Engineering.
- Ask only about scope changes, production changes or unapproved destructive actions.

PROTOCOL FOR EVERY LATER TASK (this is its home):
- REQUIREMENTS AND CLOSURE:
  - Tools/Context-Engineering/loomrefinements.md owns the requirements. It is read-only: SHA-256 8139F60D0B132405EBE02124E5553CB3085A5113EDB6B1D87EF096E4F199F50E, measured 13:39:24Z. This session writes nothing under Tools/Context-Engineering.
  - The crosswalk, C:\Users\nnbfdh8\.claude\jobs\8058984e\tmp\loom-refinements-crosswalk.json, maps every spec statement to its owning task(s), and is the only home of that mapping.
  - `node C:\Users\nnbfdh8\.claude\jobs\8058984e\tmp\crosswalk.mjs list <task>` prints a task's statements verbatim; each worker brief quotes that output, and the worker reads those spec sections in full; the task description gives scope, grounding and tests.
  - `node ...\crosswalk.mjs evidence <file.json>` appends {"<id>": "<evidence>"} to each statement's evidence. Evidence names the test (file and test name) or the command with its decisive output. Record it once per task, when the task completes.
  - Plan gate: `node C:\Users\nnbfdh8\.claude\jobs\8058984e\tmp\plan-gate.mjs --tasks C:\Users\nnbfdh8\.claude\tasks\8058984e-22ea-4252-bd8e-5551551a62b9 --crosswalk <crosswalk> --spec <spec>`. Run it at each milestone end and after any task-list change; it must print `findings 0`. Its self-test is `--self-test` (11 checks). TaskUpdate cannot remove a dependency edge; the 2026-10-04 restructuring rewrote the task JSON files with a one-off script, then confirmed the result with TaskList and the gate.
  - A task completes only when each of its crosswalk statements names its evidence and its capability-register entries pass `coverage --check`. EVIDENCE_MISSING fires for a statement once every owning task is completed without evidence.
  - The spec and its labels never appear in Loom code, docs or commit messages; the crosswalk stays outside the repository. Every commit message is checked with Loom's own prohibitedMarkers (packages/core/dist) before committing.
- CONFLICTS FOUND DURING IMPLEMENTATION: a conflict between the spec, an accepted decision, a contract or the code is resolved against the accepted requirements and the owning contract. It is appended to task 2 as a numbered decision with its reason before dependent work continues. A conflict only the owner can decide stops the dependent work and is asked in one message, with a recommendation.
- SCOPE CONSTRAINTS (from the spec): product and package versions stay 1.0.0, and model, result and configuration format numbers stay 1. Nothing stores Loom's own state in a database. No compatibility shims.
- CONTRACT CHANGES after task 9:
  - The baseline is CONTRACT_DIGEST sha256:e49a6e802cb973be5fbf4c9f117c55bfe739f5eac2d82406c2744bf0c4aab2b2 (task 9, Loom 930bde4).
  - A later task that changes any input of CONTRACT_DIGEST (schemas, profiles, projection profiles, ICDs, the operation catalogue; generate.mjs) lists the definitions it changes in its CHANGED report, regenerates, and runs contract.test.js.
  - Changing a completed boundary needs a demonstrated defect. It is recorded with an impact statement (the `planChange` output: affected owners, consumers, generated artifacts, invalidated evidence) and is accepted by the configured authority: the owner, or a pre-authorized change class in the policy. It is appended to task 2.
- SAME-CHANGE DOCS: the task that changes a documented interface updates README.md, the ICDs and Docs/workflow-integration.md in the same commit.
- SHELL (owner rule): every command runs through mcp__WindowsPowershellDesktop__execute_command, never the Bash tool. A worker calls start_console with is_subagent=true and passes the agent_id on every call. Long runs use wait_for_completion. The console is Windows PowerShell 5.1: no `??`; use $script: names, and $global: inside a ForEach-Object or for-loop body. Files are written with Add-LinesToFile or the Write and Edit tools, never Set-Content or [IO.File]::WriteAllText.
- One working tree (Tools/loom, main), one implementer at a time. Reason: a shared `tsc -b` build and about 2.3–2.6 GB of free memory. Read-only work may overlap.
- WORKERS (owner working rules, 2026-10-04):
  - One-round briefs. Before dispatch, grep the spec for the task's tables, routes and numbers, resolve every contract gap the task touches, and name each decision the worker may meet. The worker returns DECISION_NEEDED rather than guessing.
  - Warm reuse. One implementer (loom-worker, on the model the task names) is resumed across a whole milestone. Send the next task's brief right after verifying the previous one. Do the bookkeeping while the worker runs, and append each task's result once.
  - Every brief restates the Rules of Tools/loom/CLAUDE.md (and of apps/designer/CLAUDE.md for designer work), this protocol, the task scope and grounding, and the quoted crosswalk statements, and says "never use the Agent, Workflow, SendMessage, Bash or built-in PowerShell tools". The return contract is a Builder report.
  - Only code-heavy tasks are delegated; the orchestrator does the rest itself.
  - Always one worker (owner rule, 2026-10-05: "Atleast one agent always needs to work irrespective of resource consumption - being aware that some actions may take longer / need more retires."). At least one worker is running at all times: the next round or task is dispatched as soon as the previous report is filed, whatever the host load, and a spawn advisory about low headroom does not delay it. The job's context limit (workerContextLimitTokens 200000) sets when a fresh worker replaces a resumed one.
- TESTS AND EVIDENCE (owner working rules, 2026-10-04):
  - Evidence once. When its change is final, the worker runs `node C:\Users\nnbfdh8\.claude\jobs\8058984e\tmp\evidence.mjs stamp <task>`, then runs the task's AREA TESTS with `--test-reporter=tap --test-reporter-destination=C:\Users\nnbfdh8\.claude\jobs\8058984e\evidence\<task>\<suite>.tap`. Non-node checks (build, smoke, docs, coverage, core battery) go to `<name>.log` beside them, with the decisive line.
  - The orchestrator runs `node ...\evidence.mjs check <task>`. It refuses a stamp whose HEAD or working-tree hash no longer matches the tree, and a TAP older than the stamp. It prints every TAP file's tests, pass, fail and skipped counts. The orchestrator reads those counts and the decisive lines in the logs, then reruns one suite of its own choosing.
    - The working-tree hash is `git write-tree` over a temporary index after `git add -A`. On a clean tree it equals HEAD^{tree}; verified 2026-10-04 at 930bde4.
  - Host load (owner rule, 2026-10-05, quoted under WORKERS; it supersedes the 2026-10-04 rule that ran the LocalDB, designer and Playwright suites only below 70% CPU). Every suite runs whatever the load. No ledger check is declared `heavy`, because the ledger's CPU gate (ledger.mjs:525, `avg >= cpuLimitPercent`) holds only heavy checks and would hold them at any limit on a host reading 100%. Time limits are about three times the duration measured under load. A run that times out is run again with a longer limit, and every attempt is reported with its duration and CPU samples; a run that fails is investigated and fixed, never rerun until green.
  - No full suite before task 28. Core battery: node -e "import('./packages/core/dist/index.js').then(m=>m.selfTest())". A change that alters a type the designer compiles against also runs the designer build and tests.
- DONE also means:
  - every new guard fires in a test (CONTRADICTIONS, a diffs.ts case, positive and negative fixtures);
  - every new definition has additionalProperties:false and repository-relative paths, with a negative fixture;
  - every documented non-obvious constraint states its reason;
  - no internal labels and no scratch files;
  - every commit builds, and a contract that replaces an existing shape lands with the code that switches to it.
- COMMIT AND PUSH (decision 8):
  - The orchestrator commits once per task after verification; the commit is mandatory. Then it runs `git push`. A failure is recorded and ignored.
  - Since 2026-10-04 the superproject registers Tools/loom as a submodule (branch main; commit e068e24, at owner request). After a Loom push, bump only the Tools/loom gitlink in the superproject: stage nothing else, because other sessions keep uncommitted edits there (.gitmodules branch lines, CLAUDE.md, .claude/rules, other submodule checkouts). Use `git update-index --cacheinfo 160000,<loom head>,Tools/loom`, commit "chore(loom): advance Loom pointer - <subject>", and `git push`. If origin/main moved, `git merge --no-edit origin/main` first. Never rebase with an autostash over those edits. Do not run Scripts/Bump-Submodules.ps1 for this, because it re-pins every ours submodule, including other sessions'.
activeForm: Confirming peer finished and recording baseline

metadata.ownerRuleNoAgents: 2026-10-05, owner: "Once the current Worker is back, Could you not use agents any more and do all of the remaining tasks yourself ?" From the return of task 14's final-round worker (a7ffc36d22109cf12, dispatch 4976b906) on, the orchestrator dispatches no subagent and implements, verifies and commits every remaining task itself; it supersedes the WORKERS section's delegation and warm-reuse rules and every task's WORKER line. The ledger brief names this session as the agent.
metadata.resumeImprovements: From the 2026-10-05 churn analysis (task 14: 16.5 h wall, of which 5.5 h blocked on one shell pipeline that never returned and 1.7 h laptop sleep; edits wrote 4,239 lines for 2,304 net, ratio at most 1.8): on resume (1) keep a watchdog that checks every 20-30 min that work is still moving, and stops and restarts a hung shell instead of waiting; (2) give each task's ledger suite file only its area suites plus build, core battery and docs, not all 13 checks; (3) keep the host awake during runs. Remaining work was estimated at about 67-122 active hours over 23 tasks (459 statement ownerships at 6-12 min each plus about 1 h of ledger checks per task); re-estimate after task 21 is done without agents.
